chapters.title: Chapter 5780: Time! II
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
The twelve Provenance Lifeforms did not run!

Twelve foreign Provenance Lifeforms, standing at the base of a statue of time, had felt four beings appear out of nothing at their backs, and not one of them flinched toward flight. Instead they turned and spread, and came unhurried across the storming ground.
At their front walked a woman with hair the color of old bronze, bound back hard against her skull. Her eyes had held one expression for so long that Noah doubted they remembered any other.
She wore a coat of layered grey that the storms of time slid off without touching, and she moved like a magistrate carrying a sentence already written.
"You newcomers will be smart to leave," she said.

"This Elsedimension, and every Relic in it, has been claimed by THE Vheldrani Provenance Lineage. Claimed across ages. We have paid the toll on this place a hundred times over, in blood and in years, and it is ours by every weaving that binds a thing to a claim."

Her bronze eyes moved across the four of them and dismissed them in the moving. "You are trespassers on a hunt that was old before your Lineages had names. I do not know what you are. I frankly do not give a damn. Get out, and take your pathetic selves with you before we decide the trespass is worth the trouble of correcting."
Behind her, the eleven spread wider, and the storms of time bent around them as their Provenance buzzed and distored the surrounding Existence!
Noah looked at the twelve, and their measures opened to him.
|VHELDRANI PROVENANCE LIFEFORM| |VERITAS: 211. POTENTIA: 208. PONDUS: 214. PROVENANCE: 219.|

The woman was the strongest of them. The low two hundreds. The eleven behind her were less, all of them dense and self-made and genuinely grand by the measure of everything he had spent his whole climb fighting, and all of them beneath his own current standing by a distance where the number of it stopped meaning anything.

He had crossed six hundred not long ago! He grew forty to eighty more with every turn of Existence whether he lifted a finger or not. And twelve beings in the low two hundreds had come to shoo him away?
He looked at that and found it faintly, coldly amusing.
"You have made a mistake,"Noah said.
The bronze-haired woman’s eyes narrowed.
"Hey, I really dont want to have a back and forth as it has gotten very cold recently. The mistake is yours as the best you can do is leave."

"Not that mistake." Noah lifted a hand, unhurried. "You looked at me, and you decided what I was, and you did it quickly, because your people decide things quickly. That is the mistake. You should have looked just a bit longer."
"I have looked long enough to know you are one and we are twelve."
"You have looked long enough to count us. You have not looked long enough to understand that the count does not matter. Even if there were a million of you, the count still would not matter."
WAA!
And he dreamed!
WAA!

His Provenance came off him, blue and gold, and it did not fall on them as an attack falls. It rose around them slowly, and the twelve moved to shed it as they would shed any hostile weaving, and found nothing to shed, because there was nothing hostile in it! It was only a dream, settling over them, asking their existences to agree.
"What is this?!" the woman said, and for the first time her voice held a sense of alarm!
"I dreamed of you," Noah said, "as statues."
The rivers of his Provenance closed!

There was no tearing, no burning, no unmaking. Noah simply dreamed that these twelve foreign Provenance Lifeforms were frozen figures, drifting statues, silent and still and carried forever on the currents of existence, and existence agreed!
The bronze-haired woman had time to open her mouth.

Then the grey of her coat turned to stone, and the bronze of her hair with it! The expression her eyes had worn for an age set hard and stayed, and the certainty in them was the last thing to freeze, still there and cold when the rest of her had already gone still. She did not fall, because there was no down to fall in.
She hung where she had stood, turning very slowly in the storms of time, a magistrate of stone holding a sentence she would never finish reading!
Eleven more went the same, one after another, mid-step, mid-spread, mid-thought!

Twelve statues where twelve claims had stood, drifting apart on the currents, growing smaller toward the far purple, not one of them having landed a single word of protest that existence had bothered to hear.
It was very quiet afterwards!
"Hmm," Atlas said.
Noah was already moving ahead!

He crossed the storming ground toward the base of the serpent, toward the purple barrier of time that hung across the way like a curtain of years, the barrier the twelve had spent who knew how long failing to cross.
He stopped before it, and did not touch it. His gaze went instead to the ring on his own finger, and he waited.
The ring shone!

Atlas’s light poured out along Noah’s hand and into the curtain, and the curtain knew it. The same hand had made both, keyed to the same maker, and the barrier parted before that key. The years drew back. A path opened into the coil of the serpent, dim and cold and older than the storms outside it!
They went in!
Inside the serpent, time waited.

The walls of the coil were stone that was not quite stone, dark and smooth, threaded through with faint lines of light that pulsed slow, like something very large breathing in its sleep! The path curved away ahead of them, spiraling down toward a core they could not yet see, and the deeper they went the quieter it became, until the only sounds were their own passage and that slow pulse in the walls.
Noah walked at the front, and he spoke as they walked, quiet, to the old man of light beside him.
"The Vheldrani were open to me when their Dreams ceased," he said. "Their memories, at least what they were thinking of when they died."
"And?" Atlas said.
"They did not come here on their own. They were sent to this place, to strip it of your Relics at the behest of another."
Atlas was quiet for a moment. "Whose behest?"
"THE SLEEPLESS FIEND."
The light in the walls pulsed once, twice, in the silence, and when the old man started forward again the warmth had gone out of his voice.
"Okay. Anything else?"Atlas said. "Tell me the rest."

"This is not their first hunt in your Elsedimensions. They have taken things from you across the ages in different Elsedimensions. Small things. Tools. Fragments. The Fiend has been picking your bones a very long time, one Relic at a time, and paying Lineages of Provenance Lifeforms to do so."
Atlas nodded for a moment.
"The small things they can take. I expected that. Let him have every workbench and every failed prototype and every clever little toy I left lying around, and much good may they do him."
The light in the walls steadied and hardened.

"But the truly critical things, Dreamer. The things I hid in the deep places, behind curtains of years, in the coils of serpents that eat their own tails. Those were never supposed to be grasped. Not by him. Not by anyone. One of them is here. THE Quill of Chronos."
Noah listened intently.

"I made a great many things in my life," Atlas said. "Most of them were cleverness for its own sake. Cleverness is worth having for its own sake. But a few of them were more. A few of them were what I built once I understood, finally, what I was up against, and how badly I was losing."

The light pulsed beside him. "THE Quill of Chronos is one of those. With it, I wrote an inscription. A single inscription, into the weaving of an Elsedimension, and that inscription twisted time itself to my favor. Do you understand what a being could do who could write time?"
"I am beginning to,"Noah said. He thought of a serpent eating its own tail, and a place where hours blew past like seconds.
"You built this whole Dimension around the Quill, yes?"

"I built this whole Dimension to hide the Quill, and to hide the inscription I wrote with it, and to keep both out of the hands of beings who would use them to do to existence what I only ever did to a single Elsedimension."

Atlas’s voice dropped. "And now a Lineage sent by THE SLEEPLESS FIEND has found the door to it. Because they were here, THE Sleepless Fiend should sense something. I built these Elsedimensions to keep his kind out, specifically his kind, and he has never once set foot in one, which means he cannot simply follow us in. But nothing is guaranteed. Nothing has ever been guaranteed in existence. You saw that with the Vasiliou Provenance Lineage"
"Then we move quickly," Noah said.
"Yes. We get the Quill. We get out."

The old man of light almost smiled. "And then, Dreamer, and only then, you can play at inducing Roots and dreaming impossibilities to your heart’s content. But first, my Quill. Before the winter and Immense Ones and everything else in existence remembers this place is here."

Noah looked down the spiraling path, into the deep of the serpent, and the slow light pulsed in the walls, and somewhere far below, at the core they could not yet see, something old and precise waited for the first hand in an age that had a right to it.
He did not intend to walk the whole of that path as he had a faster way now.
"I dream," Noah said, quiet, "that we do not have to search for long. That the Relic is close. That we are coming up on it now."
WAA!
|25 Provenance Essence expended.|
|You have dreamed a shortening of the way as you bypass many traps of time. Existence is adjusting to agree.|
|The distance between you and THE Quill of Chronos has begun to collapse toward zero...|

The spiraling path blurred! The slow light in the walls streamed past, faster and faster, the coil unwinding around them, the core rushing up to meet them, and the four of them dissolved forward into the deep of the serpent of time!

chapters.title: Chapter 5781: Impossibilities! I
paragraphs: The core of the serpent was a storm that did not move.

Or rather, it moved in a way that had nothing to do with going anywhere. The four of them stood at the mouth of a chamber vaster than the coil that had brought them to it, and across the whole of that chamber ran rivers.

Rivers of time. They wheeled in slow circles around the center, ring inside ring, dozens of them, each one a current of raw Dimensionality of Time given a shape and a course, and where a river passed near the wall the stone aged a thousand years in an instant and un-aged a thousand more as the current curved away.

One ring ran forward. The next ran back. The next ran forward again, faster, and the air between them shimmered where the two speeds met, so that a mote of dust caught in the seam might be young on one side of itself and ancient on the other.
At the very center, held in the still eye where all the rings turned around nothing, a quill spun!

It was purple shading toward gold, no larger than a feather from a large bird, and it turned end over end in the emptiness at the heart of the storm, and it was the most patient thing Noah had ever looked at.
Everything in that chamber raged. The quill only turned, slow and even, as though it had all the time there had ever been, which, Noah understood, was very nearly the case.
"There," Atlas said. An old man made of light, standing at the mouth of a storm he had built. "THE Quill of Chronos. Exactly where I left it."
Rose looked at the wheeling rings watched intently. Achilles stood very still, watching the currents with an attention Noah had not seen on him before.
"I did not hide it behind a lock,"Atlas said. "Locks are for things you expect a clever being to reach. I hid it behind time itself."

He gestured at the rings, and the light of him flickered where a current passed. "Every one of those rivers is Dimensionality of Time. Walk into them, and they will spend you and revert you for millions and billions of years with the degradation of Time itself. They will pour age into you until there is nothing of you left that has not already happened, and then they will keep pouring, and you will be a thing that was, and never quite is."
"It works on nearly anything. When I set it turning, I judged it strong enough to drain a being approaching the level of an Immense One."

The old man’s light dimmed. "But time did not sit still while I was gone. The rivers have been turning for ages, and a river of time that turns for ages grows deeper. Whatever I set them to drain when I built this place, they would drain something grander now. I do not know how much grander."
He looked at the rings for a long moment.
"My weavings here cannot carry us through that,"Atlas said as he turned toward Noah.
"So, you may have to put in some work again."
Noah looked at the rings, and began to gather himself for the crossing!
But at this time...
"Can I be of use,"Achilles said, "and not just stand at the back?"
Noah turned.
The Emperor King had stepped forward a pace, his crystalline eyes fixed on the wheeling rivers, and there was a hunger in his stillness that had nothing to do with battle.
"I wanted the first thing I assimilated after THE Sealed One to be grand," Achilles said.
"I have not taken anything into myself since you cut the old monster loose."
He nodded at the storm. "This... seems grand. Heavy Dimensionality of Time, grown stronger across the ages, strong enough to spend something nearing an Immense One. I would like to try."
Noah considered him.

He was curious, in truth. THE Sealed One had wanted this Factor of Assimilation badly enough, and Noah had cut it free without yet seeing it used on anything worth using it on. A river of time that could drain a near-Immense being was worth using it on!
"Try," Noah said.
Achilles walked toward the storm.

He did not rush it. He crossed the floor of the chamber toward the outermost ring at an even pace, a young king in a coat of shifting color, and Rose took a half-step after him and then made herself stop with eyes filled with worry.
The first river caught him before he touched it!
Its influence reached out ahead of the current itself, and where it fell on Achilles his existence began to age! It happened without violence, without a sound. The young king’s face lined.

The color went out of his shifting coat, greying at the edges. His shoulders drew down, and his stride shortened, and by the time he stood a single pace from the raging river he was not a young king anymore!
He was an old man, bent and thin and worn, with a thousand extra years hanging off him that had arrived in the space of ten steps, and Rose clenched her fists!
Achilles reached the river. He lifted one aged, trembling hand toward it.
"Assimilate."
The word came out of him slow and cracked, an old man’s whisper, and the vibrant river of time buzzed at the sound of it.

Then it went out, not aside and not around, but into him! The whole raging ring of Dimensionality of Time buzzed once, a rising note, and poured into the old man’s outstretched hand and up his arm and down into the deep of him, the current unwinding from its course and vanishing into his existence entirely, until where a river had turned there was only empty air, and the ring inside it wheeled on as though nothing had been taken from beside it.
Noah watched, and read the body of the thing that had been an old man!

The age was already reversing. The moment the river entered him, the years it had poured into him found somewhere else to go, absorbed and reweighted and made a part of the whole, and Achilles’s bent frame straightened, the lines smoothing out of his face, the color returning to his coat, the young king coming back up out of the old one like how a drowned man comes up out of a river.
The snow in the surroundings whipped down heavily!
By the time he lowered his hand he was himself again, young-faced and ancient-eyed, and he did not stop.
On to the next river. He would Age, he would whisper, he would assimilate and come back young, and move again. Then the next!

One after another, Achilles Adrastia crossed the storm of time, and it was the strangest crossing Noah had ever watched. Every river spent him, and every river he took, and with each one the taking came easier, because his existence was becoming the thing it swallowed. By the sixth river he barely aged at all approaching it. By the ninth, the influence that had bent him double at the first ring passed over him like a draft through an open door.

Noah’s own eyes had grown heavy with time. Standing near so much raw Dimensionality of Time, even from the outside, even untouched, pressed a weight of ages against his existence, and he held it off with his Root seamlessly.
By the last river, there was nothing left to spend.

Noah looked at Achilles as he approached the final raging ring, and his sight told him a thing he had not expected. The signature of Achilles’s existence and the signature of the river had become the same. Not similar.The same.
The Emperor King had assimilated so much Dimensionality of Time that he no longer read as a being standing near a river of time. He read as a river of time that had learned to walk!
The last current did not age him at all!

Achilles stood before it, whole and young, and lifted his hand, and did not whisper. He did not need to. He waved his fingers, once, an easy motion, and the last river of Dimensionality of Time uncoiled from its ancient course and came to him, flowing and dancing around his hand like water poured over stone, curling between his fingers, before it too sank into him and was gone!
The storm was over, the chamber gone still.
Where dozens of rivers had wheeled around a spinning quill, there was only air, and a young king standing at the center of where they had been, shining.

His whole body held a stellar purple luster now, deep and slow and terrible! A light that pulsed the way the walls of the coil had pulsed, like something very large breathing in its sleep. He looked at his own hands, and then he looked up, past the empty air, at nothing Noah could see.
"It is not a river," Achilles said quietly. "I always thought it was a river. Everyone does. You stand in it, and it carries you, and one day it carries you off."

He turned his shining hands over."It is not a river. It is a room. I have been standing in one room my whole existence, thinking the walls were moving, and they were not moving. And now I have taken the room into myself, and I can feel the shape of it, and it has doors I never knew were there."
His ancient eyes came down to Noah’s. "I... did not know time had so many doors."
HUUM!
Noah floated forward.
His eyes lingered on Achilles for a moment!
"The Dimensionality you just assimilated,"Noah said, "may be enough to serve as the basis of your own Chorionic Gonadotropin. Get ready to use it soon."

He then crossed the still air to the center of the chamber, to the empty eye where the storm had turned, and there the quill still spun, patient, purple and gold, waiting. He reached the place where it turned and looked at it, and the weaving of it opened to him.
|THE QUILL OF CHRONOS|
|A Relic of the engineer known as ATLAS. Function: The inscription of Time.|
|With it, an inscription may be written into the weaving of a place that bends the flow of Time to the writer’s favor.|
|Origin: ??????|
|Remaining capacity: ??????|
|Further functions: ??????|

Half of what it was would not resolve! Question marks sat where the deeper truth of the thing hid behind a wall Noah could not yet read. It did not matter. Atlas would know, and Noah had not come to read the thing. He had come to take it.

A bubble of the Provenance of THE Human Dreamer closed around the quill, and it stopped spinning, held in a dream of stilness, and the whole chamber went quiet in a new way, as though the last turning thing in it had finally been allowed to rest!
He did not intend to linger in a place a dead man had warned him Immense Ones might sense.
"Let’s go."
He imposed his Provenance around all four of them, and the core of the serpent of time was gone!
The Glacial Elsedimension Mountain rose white and endless out of the deep of Lucy’s Legacy, and the snow never stopped falling on it.
It was a mountain that was also a sealed reality, and it climbed higher than a mountain had any right to, its slopes pale and clean and softened under a blanket of snow.

Near its shoulder, where the slope leveled into a wide white shelf, stood a monastery. It had been built out of golden Existential Conduits, the veins of existence coaxed into walls and a low roof and a single arched door, and the gold of it glowed warm and steady through the falling white, the one warm thing in a world of cold and quiet.
Snow gathered on its roof and did not melt.
Snow filled the air around it, drifting slow and soundless, each flake catching the gold of the walls as it fell, so that the monastery sat inside a slow golden storm of its own light!
Nothing moved on that mountain but the snow.
Nothing sounded but the snow, which made no sound at all. It was the most peaceful place in all of existence!
And Noah sat outside the monastery in the middle of it, on the white shelf, and let the snow fall on his crystalline shoulders and did not brush it off.
A golden bubble of light bloomed in the air before him soon after.

It held a spinning quill, held still. And a breath after it appeared, two more shapes came into being on the snow beside it. A green-haired woman and the king who shone with the luster of a hundred assimilated rivers of time. Noah nodded to them.
"Welcome to the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity," Noah said. "It is...somewhat safe here. As safe as anywhere is, now."
Rose looked at the falling snow, at the golden monastery, at the endless white slope, and for the first time since the orchard, her shoulders came down from around her ears!

Achilles did not look at any of it. He was looking at his own hands, which still pulsed with that slow stellar purple, his whole existence buzzing with Dimensionality it had not finished settling, a transformation still turning over inside him.
Noah watched him for a moment.
"Your existence is transforming," Noah said."It will keep transforming for a while yet as that makes now as good a time as any."
He rose from the snow. "Why don’t we see whether the impossible is possible?"
He had done it once already. Inducing a unique Chorionic Gonadotropin in a being already turning with fresh Dimensionality of Time could not be so much harder than that, right?

And there was more in it than kindness. A Dream of Assimilation, spun out across existence through a being who became everything he touched, was a Dream Noah would be steering. The further it spun, the more Provenance it would return to the hand that dreamed it!
He looked at the shining king in the falling snow as his eyes burned with grand ambitions!
"Sit," Noah said. "And dream with me."

sentences.text: The core of the serpent was a storm that did not move.
Or rather, it moved in a way that had nothing to do with going anywhere.
The four of them stood at the mouth of a chamber vaster than the coil that had brought them to it, and across the whole of that chamber ran rivers.
Rivers of time.

They wheeled in slow circles around the center, ring inside ring, dozens of them, each one a current of raw Dimensionality of Time given a shape and a course, and where a river passed near the wall the stone aged a thousand years in an instant and un-aged a thousand more as the current curved away.
One ring ran forward.
The next ran back.

The next ran forward again, faster, and the air between them shimmered where the two speeds met, so that a mote of dust caught in the seam might be young on one side of itself and ancient on the other.
At the very center, held in the still eye where all the rings turned around nothing, a quill spun!

It was purple shading toward gold, no larger than a feather from a large bird, and it turned end over end in the emptiness at the heart of the storm, and it was the most patient thing Noah had ever looked at.
Everything in that chamber raged.
The quill only turned, slow and even, as though it had all the time there had ever been, which, Noah understood, was very nearly the case.
"There," Atlas said.
An old man made of light, standing at the mouth of a storm he had built.
"THE Quill of Chronos.
Exactly where I left it."
Rose looked at the wheeling rings watched intently.
Achilles stood very still, watching the currents with an attention Noah had not seen on him before.
"I did not hide it behind a lock,"Atlas said.
"Locks are for things you expect a clever being to reach.
I hid it behind time itself."
He gestured at the rings, and the light of him flickered where a current passed.
"Every one of those rivers is Dimensionality of Time.
Walk into them, and they will spend you and revert you for millions and billions of years with the degradation of Time itself.
They will pour age into you until there is nothing of you left that has not already happened, and then they will keep pouring, and you will be a thing that was, and never quite is."
"It works on nearly anything.
When I set it turning, I judged it strong enough to drain a being approaching the level of an Immense One."
The old man’s light dimmed.
"But time did not sit still while I was gone.
The rivers have been turning for ages, and a river of time that turns for ages grows deeper.
Whatever I set them to drain when I built this place, they would drain something grander now.
I do not know how much grander."
He looked at the rings for a long moment.
"My weavings here cannot carry us through that,"Atlas said as he turned toward Noah.
"So, you may have to put in some work again."
Noah looked at the rings, and began to gather himself for the crossing!
But at this time...
"Can I be of use,"Achilles said, "and not just stand at the back?"
Noah turned.
The Emperor King had stepped forward a pace, his crystalline eyes fixed on the wheeling rivers, and there was a hunger in his stillness that had nothing to do with battle.
"I wanted the first thing I assimilated after THE Sealed One to be grand," Achilles said.
"I have not taken anything into myself since you cut the old monster loose."
He nodded at the storm.
"This... seems grand.
Heavy Dimensionality of Time, grown stronger across the ages, strong enough to spend something nearing an Immense One.
I would like to try."
Noah considered him.
He was curious, in truth.
THE Sealed One had wanted this Factor of Assimilation badly enough, and Noah had cut it free without yet seeing it used on anything worth using it on.
A river of time that could drain a near-Immense being was worth using it on!
"Try," Noah said.
Achilles walked toward the storm.
He did not rush it.

He crossed the floor of the chamber toward the outermost ring at an even pace, a young king in a coat of shifting color, and Rose took a half-step after him and then made herself stop with eyes filled with worry.
The first river caught him before he touched it!
Its influence reached out ahead of the current itself, and where it fell on Achilles his existence began to age!
It happened without violence, without a sound.
The young king’s face lined.
The color went out of his shifting coat, greying at the edges.
His shoulders drew down, and his stride shortened, and by the time he stood a single pace from the raging river he was not a young king anymore!
He was an old man, bent and thin and worn, with a thousand extra years hanging off him that had arrived in the space of ten steps, and Rose clenched her fists!
Achilles reached the river.
He lifted one aged, trembling hand toward it.
"Assimilate."
The word came out of him slow and cracked, an old man’s whisper, and the vibrant river of time buzzed at the sound of it.
Then it went out, not aside and not around, but into him!

The whole raging ring of Dimensionality of Time buzzed once, a rising note, and poured into the old man’s outstretched hand and up his arm and down into the deep of him, the current unwinding from its course and vanishing into his existence entirely, until where a river had turned there was only empty air, and the ring inside it wheeled on as though nothing had been taken from beside it.
Noah watched, and read the body of the thing that had been an old man!
The age was already reversing.

The moment the river entered him, the years it had poured into him found somewhere else to go, absorbed and reweighted and made a part of the whole, and Achilles’s bent frame straightened, the lines smoothing out of his face, the color returning to his coat, the young king coming back up out of the old one like how a drowned man comes up out of a river.
The snow in the surroundings whipped down heavily!
By the time he lowered his hand he was himself again, young-faced and ancient-eyed, and he did not stop.
On to the next river.
He would Age, he would whisper, he would assimilate and come back young, and move again.
Then the next!
One after another, Achilles Adrastia crossed the storm of time, and it was the strangest crossing Noah had ever watched.
Every river spent him, and every river he took, and with each one the taking came easier, because his existence was becoming the thing it swallowed.
By the sixth river he barely aged at all approaching it.
By the ninth, the influence that had bent him double at the first ring passed over him like a draft through an open door.
Noah’s own eyes had grown heavy with time.
Standing near so much raw Dimensionality of Time, even from the outside, even untouched, pressed a weight of ages against his existence, and he held it off with his Root seamlessly.
By the last river, there was nothing left to spend.
Noah looked at Achilles as he approached the final raging ring, and his sight told him a thing he had not expected.
The signature of Achilles’s existence and the signature of the river had become the same.
Not similar.The same.
The Emperor King had assimilated so much Dimensionality of Time that he no longer read as a being standing near a river of time.
He read as a river of time that had learned to walk!
The last current did not age him at all!
Achilles stood before it, whole and young, and lifted his hand, and did not whisper.
He did not need to.

He waved his fingers, once, an easy motion, and the last river of Dimensionality of Time uncoiled from its ancient course and came to him, flowing and dancing around his hand like water poured over stone, curling between his fingers, before it too sank into him and was gone!
The storm was over, the chamber gone still.
Where dozens of rivers had wheeled around a spinning quill, there was only air, and a young king standing at the center of where they had been, shining.
His whole body held a stellar purple luster now, deep and slow and terrible!
A light that pulsed the way the walls of the coil had pulsed, like something very large breathing in its sleep.
He looked at his own hands, and then he looked up, past the empty air, at nothing Noah could see.
"It is not a river," Achilles said quietly.
"I always thought it was a river.
Everyone does.
You stand in it, and it carries you, and one day it carries you off."
He turned his shining hands over."It is not a river.
It is a room.
I have been standing in one room my whole existence, thinking the walls were moving, and they were not moving.
And now I have taken the room into myself, and I can feel the shape of it, and it has doors I never knew were there."
His ancient eyes came down to Noah’s.
"I... did not know time had so many doors."
HUUM!
Noah floated forward.
His eyes lingered on Achilles for a moment!
"The Dimensionality you just assimilated,"Noah said, "may be enough to serve as the basis of your own Chorionic Gonadotropin.
Get ready to use it soon."
He then crossed the still air to the center of the chamber, to the empty eye where the storm had turned, and there the quill still spun, patient, purple and gold, waiting.
He reached the place where it turned and looked at it, and the weaving of it opened to him.
|THE QUILL OF CHRONOS|
|A Relic of the engineer known as ATLAS.
Function: The inscription of Time.|
|With it, an inscription may be written into the weaving of a place that bends the flow of Time to the writer’s favor.|
|Origin: ??????|
|Remaining capacity: ??????|
|Further functions: ??????|
Half of what it was would not resolve!
Question marks sat where the deeper truth of the thing hid behind a wall Noah could not yet read.
It did not matter.
Atlas would know, and Noah had not come to read the thing.
He had come to take it.

A bubble of the Provenance of THE Human Dreamer closed around the quill, and it stopped spinning, held in a dream of stilness, and the whole chamber went quiet in a new way, as though the last turning thing in it had finally been allowed to rest!
He did not intend to linger in a place a dead man had warned him Immense Ones might sense.
"Let’s go."
He imposed his Provenance around all four of them, and the core of the serpent of time was gone!
The Glacial Elsedimension Mountain rose white and endless out of the deep of Lucy’s Legacy, and the snow never stopped falling on it.
It was a mountain that was also a sealed reality, and it climbed higher than a mountain had any right to, its slopes pale and clean and softened under a blanket of snow.
Near its shoulder, where the slope leveled into a wide white shelf, stood a monastery.

It had been built out of golden Existential Conduits, the veins of existence coaxed into walls and a low roof and a single arched door, and the gold of it glowed warm and steady through the falling white, the one warm thing in a world of cold and quiet.
Snow gathered on its roof and did not melt.
Snow filled the air around it, drifting slow and soundless, each flake catching the gold of the walls as it fell, so that the monastery sat inside a slow golden storm of its own light!
Nothing moved on that mountain but the snow.
Nothing sounded but the snow, which made no sound at all.
It was the most peaceful place in all of existence!
And Noah sat outside the monastery in the middle of it, on the white shelf, and let the snow fall on his crystalline shoulders and did not brush it off.
A golden bubble of light bloomed in the air before him soon after.
It held a spinning quill, held still.
And a breath after it appeared, two more shapes came into being on the snow beside it.
A green-haired woman and the king who shone with the luster of a hundred assimilated rivers of time.
Noah nodded to them.
"Welcome to the Legacy of THE Acharya of Immensity," Noah said.
"It is...somewhat safe here.
As safe as anywhere is, now."
Rose looked at the falling snow, at the golden monastery, at the endless white slope, and for the first time since the orchard, her shoulders came down from around her ears!
Achilles did not look at any of it.

He was looking at his own hands, which still pulsed with that slow stellar purple, his whole existence buzzing with Dimensionality it had not finished settling, a transformation still turning over inside him.
Noah watched him for a moment.

Inducing a unique Chorionic Gonadotropin in a being already turning with fresh Dimensionality of Time could not be so much harder than that, right?

chapters.title: Chapter 5782: Impossibilities! II
paragraphs: On the Glacial Mountain, the snow continued to fall.
It lay a hand deep on the golden eaves of the monastery and drifted against the arched door, and it filled the air so completely that the far slopes had gone grey and then simply vanished.
A few Conduit Lifeforms sheltered under the roof, their light dimmed to embers.
Out on the open shelf, two figures sat facing each other, and only one of them was comfortable.
Noah wore nothing heavier than thin garments of his own Provenance, and the snow slid off his crystalline shoulders as if it had been a feather all along.
Across from him, Achilles sat buried in a coat of many-colored authorty so thick it looked like armor, and still, every little while, a shiver ran through him.
Noah closed his eyes.
His Provenance moved around him in slow blue-gold rivers, and he let himself feel all of it, the turning of his Root, the weight of his existence settling deeper into itself. What he felt was simple.
It felt good!

A human felt good after a meal, or among good company, or at the end of a day’s work that had turned out well. Understanding existence felt exactly like that to Noah. Every time he stood a little higher than the day before, the same warmth rose in him that a farmer might feel looking over a field he had planted himself.

For some, that height wore that feeling out of a climber. That past a certain point the view stopped being beautiful and became merely tiresome, and whoever stood there grew bored, and cold, and looked down on everything smaller.
And yet here he was, higher than he had ever stood, and he loved it more than ever!
He put that down to the human at the center of him.

Humanity, as far as he could tell, was the part of a being that kept being glad. Without it the climb became a hunger, and at the end of that road waited an emotionless thing. He would much rather stay the kind of being who could sit in the snow and enjoy a hard day’s work.

And this was a hard day’s work. A Root of Immensity was a thing a being had to grow for itself, by every account in existence. He meant to start one inside someone else. At home, in his Existential Root Domain, the same work had already begun with THE Infiniverse and Ruination, but they were bound to him and would come easier. Achilles was a stranger’s existence, built in a stranger’s grammar.
That was what made it worth doing!

Nothing complicated was needed. His own template, built from studying an Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin, would not be copied into the king. Instead his two Provenances would take what made Achilles himself, his genome, his Assimilation Factor above all, and press those into the shape of a signal that was Achilles’s alone.

It would only work on an existence tall enough to carry it. Below a hundred in any measure, the forming alone would tear a being apart. A Root formed on its own only somewhere near four or five hundred, in Trueness or Pondus or Provenance.
Achilles should have enough to survive the attempt!
Noah opened his eyes.
"This will strain you," he said. "It may collapse you. Whatever happens, hold on to what you are."
A smile moved at the corner of the king’s mouth, the first Noah had seen from him on the mountain."I have been holding on to what I am for weeks now, let’s go!"
Two rivers of Provenance left Noah and went into the king!

The first moved through Achilles like lamplight through a dark house, room by room, and in every room it found something that had once belonged to someone else and now belonged entirely to him. A First Cause from a fallen Observable Existences. An Infinity drunk from a dying sea. A thousand authorities, and not one of them sat in him like a stone. They had all become Achilles, as rain that falls into a river becomes the river, and at the heart of it all turned the thing THE Sealed One had wanted: the Assimilation Factor.
Noah’s second river closed around it and began to press.
He did not wrench it. He coaxed it inward, steadily, toward the turning, self-feeding form of a becoming-signal, and after a long moment of resistance, the Factor began to follow.
Light gathered at the center of the king!

A knot of many colors drew in on itself beneath the heavy coat and brightened as it drew. A quarter formed. A third. Half. For one held breath it turned bright and nearly whole, and Noah let himself think it might simply finish.
But...
It broke!
BOOM!

Dark lines split across Achilles’s existence like fractures through ice under too much weight! The signal was grander than the vessel that held it, and the vessel was coming apart, and Noah began to draw his Provenance back before the cracks could reach the edges of the man.
He never finished.

Achilles turned on the failing signal and did what he had done his whole life to everything that threatened him. He took it. He assimilated the collapsing Chorionic Gonadotropin whole, and the cracks slowed, and sealed shut.
The king lifted his head, old eyes burning as blood spurted from his nose and mouth!
"Again!"he roared into the snow. "Do it again!"
Noah pressed the Factor a second time!

It came together faster, because a piece of the first was already woven into Achilles, and it climbed past half before the dark lines came as it fell apart. The king did not wait for them to spread. He swallowed the second failure himself and bared his teeth for a third.
The third broke at two thirds, and he took it.
The fourth broke brighter, throwing the shadows of the eaves across the snow in long gold bars, and the Conduit Lifeforms woke under the roof and turned toward him.
By the fifth, the snow around the two of them had melted in a ring from sheer pressure of existence!
By the sixth, Noah’s Provenance was running hot, and Achilles’s coat had split along one shoulder, and beneath the tear his skin shone with a light that was not quite any color.
Everytime a blank Chorionic Gonadotropin tried to form, it failed!
He caught the seventh at the very edge of collapse, with a sound like a man lifting something far too heavy and refusing to set it down.
The eighth failed closer still, and he took that too!
He was heaving at this point as a distant Rose stood imperiously trying not to show any emotion!
On the ninth, the signal reached the point where every other had cracked, and...it did not crack.

There was nothing left in Achilles for it to strain against. Eight failed becoming-signals were woven into him now, and the shape was no longer a stranger to his existence. The ninth did not have to force its way in. It only had to finish.
It finished!
The Assimilation Chorionic Gonadotropin held!

A pillar of light tore out of Achilles Adrastia and struck straight up into the falling snow, every color he had ever assimilated turning through it at once! The snow above the shelf blew outward in a vast ring! The monastery’s golden walls hummed!
|An Assimilation Chorionic Gonadotropin has formed within the lifeform, Achilles Adrastia.|
|Stability: LOW. The foundation is uneven. It was built from nine attempts, and eight of them remain visible in it.|
Noah could see them now: eight ragged seams running through the turning signal, eight places where the whole of it might one day split.
So he spent more.

He ran his Provenance along the seams one by one, smoothing each into the next until they lay flat in a single foundation, and the pillar brightened as he worked! Its ragged edges drew in! Its hum deepened into something clear and certain, and the drifting flakes caught fire in a hundred colors as they fel!
His own Root had been built around a true piece of an Immense One’s becoming, pressed into his hands by Vakochev.
Achilles had no such piece, only his own Dimensionality and Noah’s help, so his Root would begin lower. But lower was not small.
Starting from a king who had swallowed the powers of a dozen lineages and a hundred rivers of time, lower was still very high indeed.
And Achilles, alongside many others, could be seen as lifeforms with their own grand dreams and stories, but it did not bother Noah for being able to help such beings.
One did not grow grander alone. Nor was it shameful for one to receive the help of another to get to where they were.
Did he not receive help from Vakochev with the Existential Chorionic Gonadotropin? Did he not help Vakochev himself to have one of his bodies freed?

He did not doubt that in time, Achilles would be able to form a Root by himself. After all, the fucker could Assimilate anything. What he was doing was giving a guiding hand and accelerating the entire process.

Nobody was alone in existence as connections made many things possible and allowed for progress to be much faster, and Dreams...connected a great deal of beings as Noah would freely do whatever he wanted to do to expand his Dream, and any dreams of those around him.
|A Root has been induced and formed in another lifeform.|
|The Assimilation Chorionic Gonadotropin has formed in the lifeform, Achilles Adrastia. It is a Unique Conceptual Root of Immensity.|
|For guiding the dream of another and allowing it to bloom to fruition, your Provenance has increased by +50.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer will continue to gain Provenance depending on how far the Dream of the lifeform, Achilles Adrastia, extends across existence.|
Yes. There was also his own selfishness as he would benefit from this!

Achilles sat inside his pillar of light with his coat torn from one shoulder, breathing hard, staring at nothing Noah could see. Something inside him had just begun to grow, and he did not yet know how large it meant to become.
Noah’s eyes shone!
He looked at the king and the pillar and the shining result of an afternoon’s work in the snow, and he saw it for what it was. A piece of glorious engineering, finished well.
Impossibilities would only remain impossibilities for others.
Not for him. Never for him!
